skill.name: prd-generator

content.value_statement: Rough product ideas often leave builders guessing about scope, screen behavior, and error messages. This skill turns those ideas into a concise specification with screen states, interface copy, and acceptance checks.
actual_capabilities: Use a three-line specification for a small change or a full PRD for a feature or new product.
Ask focused questions about the first users and the initial release, or draft immediately with stated assumptions.
Use screenshots or an existing app to identify screens and separate observations from proposed changes.
Specify first use, empty, loading, error, and success states for each screen, with exact interface text where needed.
Document user flows, business rules, release exclusions, and acceptance checks.
Break a full PRD into build steps that each cover a named screen or flow.
limitations: Does not build the app, produce visual mockups, or run acceptance checks.
Leaves layout, styling, and technology choices open unless you state them as constraints.
Does not verify market claims or user facts. It lists unverified details as assumptions for you to confirm.
Cannot infer behavior that screenshots do not show. Provide missing rules or confirm them in the draft.

use_cases.title: Define the First Release
use_cases.description: Turn an early product idea into a first-release scope with explicit exclusions and an ordered list of build steps.

use_cases.title: Specify Screen States From Screenshots
use_cases.description: Use screenshots to describe existing screens, identify missing states, and draft the text users should see.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Small Behavior Change
use_cases.description: Specify one change on an existing screen, including what users see when it succeeds or fails and how to verify it.

prompt_templates.title: Specify One Small Change
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a three-line specification for adding a retry button when the order history fails to load. Include the button text, possible outcomes, and a check for completion.
prompt_templates.scenario: A small change to one screen.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a PRD for saved searches in an existing job board. Cover only the screens that change and list what is outside the first release.
prompt_templates.scenario: A new feature in an existing product.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these screenshots to draft an updated onboarding PRD. Separate observed behavior from proposed changes. Include first-use, loading, and error states, with exact messages and acceptance checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: An existing flow with missing screen states.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an MVP Build
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an MVP PRD for a mobile shift-swap tool for retail staff. Staff can request swaps and managers can approve them. Do not ask questions. List assumptions and organize the work into build steps, each with screen states, permission rules, and acceptance checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A new product with multiple roles and a staged implementation.

output_examples.input: Add a retry button when the order history fails to load.
output: Change: Add a Try again button to the error state on Order history.
States and words: Show the order list after a successful retry. If the retry fails, show: "Order history did not load. Try again."
Done when: After a failed load, selecting Try again after the connection returns shows the order list.

output_examples.input: Draft a PRD for staff to request shift swaps and managers to approve them.
output: First release: Staff request swaps, and managers approve or decline them. Payroll integration stays out of scope.
Manager review screen: Show pending requests. When none remain, show: "No shift swaps need approval."
Acceptance check: After a manager approves a request, it disappears from the pending list and appears as approved for the staff member.
First build step: Let a staff member submit a request and see it marked as pending.

best_practices: Name the first users, their device, and the main task the first release must support.
Label screenshots by screen and supply permission rules, limits, and timeouts that the images do not show.
Confirm assumptions and check that each screen has testable acceptance criteria before implementation.
anti_patterns: Requesting a full PRD for a single label or small behavior change.
Treating first use and an empty screen as the same state.
Treating assumptions as confirmed requirements or adding features outside the agreed scope.

faq.question: What can I provide as input?
faq.answer: Start with an idea, notes, screenshots, or an existing app. Include any known scope limits and user roles.

faq.question: Will the skill ask questions before drafting?
faq.answer: It can ask up to two rounds of focused questions. Name the users and first-release goal, or ask for a draft without questions.

faq.question: When is the short form used?
faq.answer: Use the short form for one control, message, or small behavior change. It records the change, states and text, and a check for completion.

faq.question: What does a full PRD include?
faq.answer: It includes scope, assumptions, constraints, screens, flows, rules, decisions, and build order. Each screen includes relevant states and acceptance checks.

faq.question: Does it choose a visual design or technology stack?
faq.answer: No. It defines screen behavior and interface text. It records design or technology choices only when you provide them as constraints.

faq.question: Do I need an external design service?
faq.answer: No. The PRD works on its own. Ask for the PRD only to omit the optional referral.
